title: The Morning Digest: November 21, 2026
dek: Brent Jan27 settled $92.57, up $0.59, and down 3.41 percent on the week, and WTI Jan27 settled $83.41, up $0.97, on Friday (Reuters, Nov 20), with January taking over as the front month after December expired. January WCS paper settled -$21.65 (ICE TMW settle, Nov 20), tightening for a fourth straight session. Mars fell from a $10 premium to a $4 discount against WTI in under a month (Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 20), and the West Coast export pipeline is running at a record 960 kb/d in November. The validated diesel crack is $80.73 on the latest print.

sources.vintage: Nov 20, 2026 (Friday settles: Brent Jan27 $92.57, up $0.59 or 0.64 percent, down 3.41 percent on the week from $95.84 on Nov 13, a third straight weekly loss; WTI Jan27 $83.41, up $0.97, in its first session as front month; expiring WTI Dec26 $83.98, up $0.77, down 5.17 percent on the week on a December to December comparison; Brent premium over December WTI about $8.59; Brent was down about a dollar at 0900 GMT before a late gain into the settle)

Nov 20, 2026 (the Brent prompt spread weakened on Friday; factors reported for the late gain include worries about possible renewed United States strikes on Iran and short covering ahead of the Thanksgiving week; the IEA view of a roughly 2 million barrels a day surplus this quarter was cited in the same wrap)

Nov 20, 2026 (TMW Jan27 -$21.65, up $0.35 on 1 lot; Feb27 -$21.40 on 435 lots; Mar27 -$21.00 on 215 lots; Apr27 -$20.30, May27 -$18.75, Jun27 -$17.25; ARV Dec26 -$18.25 on zero lots, Jan27 -$14.00 on 1 lot, Feb27 -$13.40 on 765 lots; January ARV to TMW spread +$7.65; TMS Jan27 +$5.35 on 50 lots, TMF Jan27 +$7.00, TMR Jan27 -$0.75 on 110 lots, TMU Jan27 +$2.80)

Nov 21, 2026 (diesel crack $80.73 and 3-2-1 crack $41.00 on the latest print dated Nov 20; all time maximum diesel crack $117.92 on Sep 16; 45 total closes above $100; current streak above $100 is zero)

Nov 20, 2026 (Mars fell from a $10 premium to a $4 discount against WTI futures in less than a month, its steepest discount since late September, after a record $17.50 premium in March and April; the swing is attributed in the piece to a surge in heavy and sour supply from Canada, Venezuela and the Middle East; February Mars delivered into Northeast Asia remained about $10 a barrel above comparable Saudi oil; the pipeline carrying oil sands crude to West Coast export markets is operating at a record 960 kb/d this month, about 8 percent above stated capacity, with 34 vessels scheduled out of Westridge in November against 31 in October)

Nov 19, 2026 (Trans Mountain reported its drag reducing agent capacity project completed in October, two and a half months ahead of schedule, taking system capacity to 980 kb/d; October set records with 30 tanker sailings from Westridge and 15.9 million barrels exported, per RBC analysis dated Nov 19; the reported October completion sits ahead of the January 2027 effective date carried in the expansion tracker from the September 2026 CER application, and the two are not reconciled in this edition)

Nov 18, 2026 (December Mainline apportionment: Light 24 percent at Kerrobert, Heavy 17 percent at Kerrobert; the Cromer and Superior points for December were not retrievable in any public source on the Nov 21 check; a trade report dated Nov 18, 2026 confirms December light nominations were cut, the deepest light cut since February, with its percentages not public)

Nov 20, 2026 (the North Dakota Pipeline chloride disruption entered its seventh day on Friday, with producers trucking Bakken crude to Dakota Access Pipeline delivery points, tanks filling and trucks in short supply on an Energy Aspects read; force majeure declarations stand at Flint Hills Pine Bend and at MPLX; no restart timeline has been published)

Nov 20, 2026 (an outbound tanker was struck on the port bow by an unknown projectile eight nautical miles north of Khasab at about 15:00 UTC, caught fire, and reported no casualties; the fourth strike in the Khasab area in five days; an Iranian Revolutionary Guards claim that the tanker struck a naval mine is unverified and UKMTO has not identified the weapon); UKMTO weekly overview, reported Nov 20, 2026 (263 transits in the week ending Nov 18, down 14.6 percent on the prior week and about 65 percent below pre-conflict levels, with six tanker attacks in the week); JMIC Update 115, Nov 19, 2026 (threat level for the strait remains SEVERE)

sources.publisher: Kpler media briefing via Associated Press
sources.vintage: Nov 18, 2026 (3d old) (crude flows through the strait itself were 8.5 million barrels a day in preliminary figures through Nov 16, about 50 percent of the pre-war level, against 8,264 kb/d through Nov 11 on the prior gauge; oil moving by all routes out of the Middle East was 15.0 million barrels a day, about 64 percent of pre-war, down from 97 percent in October)
Nov 20, 2026 (Middle East exports averaged about 13 million barrels a day over Nov 1 to 14, about 20 percent below October)

Nov 21, 2026 (early Saturday the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles fired toward Riyadh, the second attack on the capital in a few days; on Friday the coalition struck Hodeidah and Houthi missile and drone capabilities in Sanaa, and the Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah and warned airlines away from Saudi airspace; no Saudi oil supply impact was reported)

Nov 20, 2026 (at his noon Eastern news conference the President said Iran wants a deal but has not offered acceptable terms, that he wants a real deal, and that he would take military action again to keep Iran from a nuclear weapon; the conference added no clarity on next steps, and his Thursday position that he is not rushing a decision until after the new year stands)

sources.publisher: Ukrainian General Staff via Kyiv Independent
sources.vintage: Nov 20, 2026 (Ukraine confirmed its Nov 19 strike hit the Kaleykino-1 pumping station near Almetyevsk, a Druzhba system hub, with three storage tanks hit, one on fire and two damaged; no throughput impact figure published); Al Jazeera, Nov 21, 2026 (a fire at the Ryazan refinery was verified on footage by the independent outlet Astra, with the regional governor reporting debris fires at industrial sites without naming the refinery); Reuters, Nov 20, 2026 (Russia launched more than 400 drones and 110 missiles against Ukrainian energy sites, bridges and grid links on Friday, by the Ukrainian president's count)

sources.publisher: EIA Weekly Petroleum Status Report for the week ending
sources.vintage: Nov 13, 2026, released Nov 18, 2026 (3d old) (crude up 3.380 million barrels to 417.797 million; gasoline up 5.129 million to 215.949 million; distillate up 1.571 million to 104.901 million; Cushing down 1.209 million to 26.147 million; refinery utilisation 95.7 percent; US production 14,032 kb/d; SPR down 3.174 million to 276.361 million, the lowest since August 1982)

Nov 20, 2026 (the weekly EIA forecast note for the week ending Nov 13, carried inside the stocks wrap: crude build forecast of 1.1 million barrels against a 3.4 million actual, gasoline up 2.5 million against 5.2 million actual, distillate up 0.6 million against 1.6 million actual, jet up 0.1 million, refinery runs holding near 17.0 million barrels a day, a large net import reduction, implied domestic supply up 0.5 million barrels a day, and a strategic reserve draw of 3.1 million barrels against about 3.2 million actual; the note's verdict on the prior week is that the Nov 6 balance realized significantly looser than expectations, with no specific line named as the miss in the republication)

Nov 20, 2026 (Rystad Energy: the Shenzhen fuel pledge offers little near-term relief, with no volume target or timetable, United States refiners already running close to capacity, Russian refinery runs slumped to about 3.5 million barrels a day in November from 4.3 million in October and 5.0 million a year ago, and China expected to hold product exports near September and October levels while it rebuilds stocks; European gasoil fell 1.5 percent on the declaration news)

Nov 20, 2026 (Alberta adjusted its carbon capture incentive program so grants covering 12 percent of eligible capital costs can flow during construction, aligning the program with the federal investment tax credit; the parties had aimed to announce definitive Pathways agreements around Nov 15 and executives have signalled they will take the time needed on terms; no signing announced)

Nov 20, 2026 (Western Canada oil-directed rigs fell nine to 153 in the week ended Nov 20, with all nine dropped rigs in Alberta, giving back most of the prior week's ten-rig gain; gas-directed rigs rose three to 70; the national oil count stands at 159, down five)

sources.publisher: Baltic Exchange tanker report, Week 47, week ending
sources.vintage: Nov 20, 2026 (VLCC Gulf to China round-trip time charter equivalent about $1,079,794 a day, essentially flat against Week 46, on a Worldscale print of WS315.63; US Gulf Coast to China VLCC lump sum about $34.5 million; Caribbean to Gulf Aframax near WS623 and US Gulf to Rotterdam Aframax above WS596; Vancouver to China Aframax lump sum eased to $8.17 million)

sources.publisher: WCSB supply and demand balance build
sources.vintage: Nov 4, 2026 (standing reference) (AER ST3 actuals through September 2026: November supply about 192 kb/d and December about 216 kb/d above the proven egress bound of 4,541.6 kb/d; the balance residual is storage, and it is not carried as a storage forecast, because the traded strip tightening on volume with an orderly location spread and a record West Coast flow rate say the residual cannot be read that way; the error sits in one of two named suspects, either the production estimates are too high or the egress capacity is too low; carried forward and checked Nov 21, 2026)

sources.publisher: US Department of Energy, checked directly
sources.vintage: Nov 21, 2026 (no new solicitation, award announcement or posted contract change dated Nov 20 or 21 found; the newest DOE item is a Nov 20 grid emergency order for a Pennsylvania generating station; the latest SPR item remains the Oct 29 award completing the 172 million barrel programme)
